text:
maya: Seeing a spike in LB retries and backend connection drops from eu-west1 around 21:03 UTC. Graphs show retries and 502s. Suspect conntrack saturation.
oncall-bot: Incident logged: INC-20260315-01. Paging oncall.
maya: Quick obs — lots of conntrack drops in kernel logs: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" repeated.
samir: Can you paste `conntrack -S` and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` output?
maya: `conntrack -S` excerpt:
```
# conntrack -S
cpu=0 drain=0
entries: 262140
searches: 1.2M
found: 1.1M
new: 55k
invalid: 2k
```
and `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` -> `262144`.
lee: That looks like saturation — count (262140) is at the max (262144). We saw a burst when the autoscaler bumped nodes + lots of short-lived connections.
karen: Yikes. Any recent kube-proxy or iptables changes?
maya: No kube-proxy config changes in last deploy. Release notes show autoscaler and app traffic increase.
samir: Immediate mitigation: bump nf_conntrack_max and add a temporary rule to drop low-value flows? Ops-sre, agree?
ops-sre: Agreed. We'll roll a sysctl change to 524288 on affected nodes first -> then make it persistent in /etc/sysctl.d/99-conntrack.conf. Command: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288`.
maya: Starting canary patch in eu-west1 cluster-3 now.
lee: Also validating netfilter counters after patch. Please run `cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `conntrack -S` again post-apply.
maya: Canary patch applied to 3 nodes, no regressions observed; retries dropped within 2 mins on canary. Rolling to remainder of cluster. :thumbsup:
ops-sre: Patch rolled to all eu-west1 nodes. Monitoring.
karen: Short-term action items: 
- temp bump nf_conntrack_max (ops-sre) — done
- monitor conntrack usage and alert on >70% (monitoring)
- validate no kube-proxy restarts required (infra)
Longer-term: autoscale conntrack table + add runbook.
samir: Assigning owners: Samir = remediation lead (autoscale + alert), Lee = kernel/runtime changes (tuning, test), Maya = postmortem and follow-ups (writeup + PRs).
maya: Filing the PRs now. Links: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/891 (sysctl persist), github.com/redwood/monitoring/pull/432 (conntrack alert).
lee: For the daemonset approach we should also expose metrics via node-exporter: `node_netfilter_conntrack_count` (or custom). I'll open a draft later today.
samir: Timeline: short-term (1h) mitigation = done. Mid-term (24h) daemonset + alert. Long-term (2w) load test + infra change to prevent recurrence. Samir ETA for daemonset: 2026-03-16 23:59 UTC.
karen: QA: create synthetic conn churn test to validate changes and prevent regressions. Maya can you coordinate with QA?
maya: Yep — scheduling a test tomorrow 09:00 UTC. I'll include steps in the postmortem draft.
oncall-bot: Reminder set: follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-16 12:00 UTC.
ops-sre: Added runbook snippet to the incident page with CLI commands and rollback notes.
samir: I'll own the alert and the Grafana panel. Adding thresholds + runbook link.
lee: Also planning kernel parameter hardening — will propose changes and testing plan.
maya: Postmortem plan: outline timeline, root cause (conntrack saturation due to connection churn + table not sized for bursty autoscale), immediate mitigations, owners, and preventive work. Draft by EOD.
ops-sre: Please add a note to track cross-region traffic patterns — similar bursts could happen in other regions under autoscale.
karen: Agreed — add an incident recurrence watch for 4 weeks.
maya: Closing loop here — will update incident doc with PR links and assign follow-up tasks after the meeting. Thanks team. :eyes:
